findings.passage: We have an opportunity to make the program workable for the State and its residents in a way that balances the rights and responsibilities of gun ownership and valid public concerns around gun safety.
findings.note: One-page handout from Rep. Chaichi's office on HB 3511, filed as public testimony in the 2023 session. It frames the bill as a way to make the Measure 114 permit-to-purchase system workable.

findings.passage: A permitting system that uses 36 different forms and processes depending on your county just doesn’t make sense for Oregon.
findings.note: From the same HB 3511 handout from the member's office. It describes moving the permit system from county sheriffs to the state transportation agency, with one statewide process, an online application, safe-storage and suicide-prevention training, and a delayed start date.

findings.passage: Moving to a permitting system, as modified by HB 3511, makes it possible for purchasers to skip the NICS check, saving money and time, and streamlining the background check process.
findings.note: From the same HB 3511 handout. It says an annual permit check would also flag people whose right to have a gun has been restricted by a felony conviction.
